description: The bar chart titled “QLoRA” illustrates the GPU memory usage (in GB) for various fine-tuning methods applied to the Llama-3-8B model across ten NLP tasks, as compared in the paper “Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets.” The vertical y-axis represents GPU Memory in GB, ranging from 0 to over 60, with major gridlines at 0, 20, 40, and 60. The horizontal x-axis lists six methods: “Full FT,” “MTL-FT,” “TAG,” “LoRA,” “QLoRA,” and “Ours,” each represented by a vertical bar. The first five bars are orange, while the final bar, labeled “Ours,” is green, visually distinguishing the proposed method. “Full FT” consumes the most memory, at approximately 70 GB. “MTL-FT” follows at about 40 GB, “TAG” and “LoRA” each use around 23–25 GB, and “QLoRA” uses roughly 15 GB. The “Ours” method uses approximately 24 GB, slightly more than QLoRA but significantly less than Full FT or MTL-FT. The chart visually supports the caption’s claim that the proposed method incurs only 9 GB more memory than QLoRA (which uses ~15 GB), aligning with the stated 24 GB usage, while achieving improved accuracy with substantially lower computation than Full FT.
